searchText: b"h final handoff — unified awtsmoos movie system the awtsmoos makes many vessels without surrendering the one from which their powers flow; awtsmoos.com now lets each studio keep its character while one movie language teaches all of them to know. what exists now awtsmoos studio apps/awtsmoos studio is a real unified movie application rather than a decorative shell. it uses the shared declarative awtsmoosui runtime and the shared canvas movie renderer. it supports: real play / pause; deterministic seeking; scene navigation; canonical project json loading; plain language ai movie direction; responsive canvas preview; 180 second canonical showcase loading; mobile first transport and timeline behavior; procedural movie capability discovery; real native procedural asset invocation through awtsmoos procedural core. shared movie truth the movie contract remains renderer neutral. the canonical acceptance project is 180 seconds across 18 scenes with broad semantic feature and camera coverage. studio playback, adapter projection, and proof rendering operate from shared movie concepts rather than independent app specific story formats. awtsmoos procedural core libs/awtsmoos procedural core/src/core/movie/ is the common movie/procedural gateway. it exposes portable asset generation plus lazy native systems including humans, mesh text, creatures, rocks, particles/effects, buildings, and textures. the intent is deliberate: ai learns one safe vocabulary, while renderer capable studios may execute the real native generator modules instead of hallucinating unsupported capabilities. five product personalities one canonical movie now projects into five intentionally different surfaces: 1. animator — shots, plans, cinematic/spatial workflow, legacy compatibility aliases. 2. mitzvah studio — editable 2d documents/canvas semantics. 3. nesher studio — nle style clips/scenes and editing workflow. 4. video editor — timeline clip projection. 5. awtsmoos slides — presentation oriented editable elements, with spatial/3d layers preserved as deferred canonical metadata. the adapter acceptance suite ensures unification does not collapse these products into one identical shell. real three minute proof final full movie: apps/animator/proofs/three minute unified showcase/awtsmoos unified three minute showcase.mp4 measured properties: 180.000000 seconds; h.264 video; aac audio; 640x360; 2 fps completion render sampling; 360 freshly rendered temporal samples; 3,948,519 bytes; seven of seven widely separated sample frames have distinct sha 256 hashes; audio is non silent (mean 40.9 db, max 3.8 db). the original canonical exporter still defaults to 12 fps. a dedicated completion entrypoint lowers only proof sampling to 2 fps because direct measured throughput showed the full 2,160 frame pass was impractical on the available machine. duration, scene timing, semantic movie content, camera choreography, overlays, and audio timing remain the complete 180 second project. detailed proof lives beside the mp4 in completion verification.md. browser / mobile proof the real studio was exercised through an owned chrome target: desktop layout had no horizontal overflow; mobile emulation near 390x844 had no horizontal overflow; the logical 640x360 canvas scaled responsively; live playback reached 180.0 / 180s; ai generated a real 24 second hybrid movie; seek moved to 12.0 / 24s; reset restored 0.0 / 180s; corrected cdp smoke captured zero runtime exceptions. mobile screenshot: apps/awtsmoos studio/proofs/mobile 390x844.png final test evidence studio: 5/5 pass. shared movie: 12/12 pass. media verifier/exporter regression: 3/3 pass. awtsmoosui: 1/1 pass. syntax: pass. touched js/test files <=120 lines: pass. tab indentation gate: pass. focused final receipt cleanup: exit 0. failures that improved the system the old supposed three minute mp4 was only 63.833333 seconds and was rejected. a four minute worker envelope killed an otherwise healthy 12 fps offline render; the infrastructure diagnosis prevented a false renderer bug fix. a later full 12 fps attempt proved real throughput was too slow for bounded completion on the available hardware. the successful 2 fps media initially failed only because the verifier hardcoded 12 fps. that exposed a second hidden bug: exporter receipts hardcoded 2,160 frames. both assumptions are now plan driven and regression tested. operational notes the 2 fps mp4 is an acceptance/proof artifact, not a claim of theatrical production frame rate. the architecture still supports higher fps when hardware/runtime performance permits it. the canonical movie contract and the default exporter remain independent of the completion sampling override. node emitted inherited module typeless package json warnings for some es modules during tests. they did not cause failures and are outside this movie system acceptance surface; no package level rewrite was performed merely to silence informational warnings in a heavily concurrent repository. takeover state a future developer should begin from the shared movie contract and procedural gateway rather than adding another app local movie schema. product specific differences belong in adapters/renderers. new ai generation features should compile into canonical semantic layers, then capability planning should decide which studio renders natively, falls back, or preserves handoff metadata. completion state all user requested implementation and verification gates tracked by this mission are closed. the only future work is optional evolution—higher performance production rendering, additional adapters/features, or package warning cleanup—not unfinished acceptance work from this request.

searchText: b"h boruch hashem blessed is he phase one — evidence first repair the awtsmoos makes the current source the witness, not yesterday's test; awtsmoos.com improves when each contract follows the real owner best. observed facts: searchapp.js owns document.body.dataset.searchactive = 'true'. searchcontroldisclosure.js creates .library search options and inserts it before the search button. form.css is therefore a three column desktop shell: query, options, action. form disclosure.css expands opened advanced options across the form. the stale test still reads script.js and requires the retired four column layout. plan: 1. rewrite only the presentation contract. 2. keep production source unchanged unless tests/browser evidence proves a defect. 3. preserve active search, vertical mobile context, asset version, and small module assertions. 4. verify the contract itself remains <=120 lines.
